 Critical PHP updates on Oct. 21 fix code injection vulnerabilities
 Technical details are due at 4 p.m., but the situation is serious: Remote code execution is possible. Admins should weigh the risk.
 listen 
 Print view
 (Image: janews / Shutterstock.com)
 at 11:14 am CEST
 1 min. read
 Security
 By
 Dr. Christopher Kunz 
 Advertisement
 At 4 p.m. Central European Summer Time (2 p.m. UTC) on Oct. 21, the PHP project will release an update for the open-source web scripting language that fixes two critical security vulnerabilities. The announcement appears on the PHP project website. Admins should act as soon as the packages are released; the vulnerabilities allow arbitrary code to be executed remotely over the internet.
 Continue after ad
 Several organizations, including CERT-EU , are warning subscribers about the vulnerabilities and urging them to install updates promptly. They are withholding technical details for now. Heise Security has obtained those details and will publish them at 4 p.m.
 Videos by heise
 mehr Videos
 c't 3003
 heise & ct
 Peertube
 Only an update will fix it
 A circulating proof-of-concept exploit cannot be reproduced in a lab environment and is designed to work only with one server API — LiteSpeed’s (“lsphp8”). However, the details about the vulnerabilities due out this afternoon apply to every PHP version since PHP 5. The purported mitigation, session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 , is also ineffective, according to our understanding.
 For now, admins must wait for Linux distributions to release PHP package updates, which will hopefully be available soon, and install them promptly. Working exploits are likely to emerge within hours, or a day at most. Anyone unwilling to risk a compromise has only one option left: disconnect PHP-powered web servers from the internet.
